reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) discusses self-regenerative perovskites and reverse sintering on Mo2N supports, but none provides direct support for the key premises that a thin surface oxide layer on generic transition-metal catalysts reduces sintering while maintaining activity. The premises are therefore largely unsupported by the specific prior evidence provided.
premises: A thin surface oxide layer on metal nanoparticles can act as a kinetic barrier to reduce sintering.
The oxide layer can maintain or enhance catalytic activity/selectivity by preserving active sites.
The oxide layer can fine-tune electronic environment and binding energies per Sabatier principle.
Controlled oxidation pretreatment is effective for transition-metal catalysts under high-temperature redox conditions.
